top_categories.workout_context: 70 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Chile's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
72ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
5,099ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
At Gran Fondo Chile, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Gran Fondo Chile's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 70 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Chile. Train it until it feels boring.
Base fitness for Gran Fondo Chile. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
5,099ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,099ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work for 5,099ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on mixed terrain. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.

race_overlay.heat: October in Lago Ranco, Los Rios, Chile can bring heat. If the forecast warrants it, include controlled heat exposure before Gran Fondo Chile and rehearse the drinking and electrolyte plan you tolerate in training. Do not introduce a fixed sodium protocol solely from this preview.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Chile’s 70 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at Gran Fondo Chile. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 70 miles of mixed terrain in Lago Ranco, Los Rios, Chile.
